content: The enzyme known as DHRS1 (Dehydrogenase/Reductase SDR family member 1), also referred to as Short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase family 19C member 1, is encoded by the DHRS1 gene in humans. This gene is located on chromosome 14, specifically in the 14.3 region, and consists of 9 exons. The protein encoded by this gene is composed of 314 amino acids and has a molecular weight of approximately 33 kDa. It is believed to be localized within the endoplasmic reticulum and the inner mitochondrial membrane of the cell. The DHRS1 protein is hypothesized to exhibit oxidoreductase activity, based on its sequence similarity and the presence of conserved catalytic sites shared with other short-chain oxidoreductase enzymes. This enzyme has been observed to be expressed in the fetal brain. The DHRS1 protein is also thought to interact with another protein, phospholipid scramblase 1 (PLSCR1).
